First, note that $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{12}{3})$ means the same thing as ${}_{12}{C}_{3}.$

 In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=12$ and $r=3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{12}{C}_{3} & =\frac{12!}{(12-3)!3!} \\  & =\frac{12!}{9!3!} \\  & =\frac{12\cdot 11\cdot 10\cdot \cancel{9!}}{\cancel{9!}\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{12\cdot 11\cdot 10}{6} \\  & =220.\end{aligned}
$$
